Annualized revenue and future compute commitments cannot substitute for realized annual totals. The broader economic-presence language is not resolved by these figures.
limitations: The two numerical metrics must not be combined into one monetary total.

No exact tolerance for the approximate forecasts was supplied.

statement.excerpt: While their existence supports the overall symbolic value of the US stock market, their actual economic presence is minor, outside of what I estimate is around $75 billion to $100 billion of 2026 compute spend and what will likely be around $60 billion of combined revenue, with the rest of the AI industry having so little that it’s barely worth thinking about.

from_speaker: around $75 billion to $100 billion of 2026 compute spend
what will likely be around $60 billion of combined revenue
their actual economic presence is minor
the rest of the AI industry having so little
our_interpretation: Assess the two numerical forecasts separately: combined OpenAI and Anthropic compute spending, and combined revenue earned during calendar 2026.
'I estimate' and 'will likely' express uncertainty; they are not antecedent conditions.
Compute spending ordinarily includes training and serving models, but excludes unrelated spending and commitments for future years.
Revenue means revenue earned during the year, not an annualized revenue run rate.
No numerical tolerance is supplied for 'around'. A boundary case requires clarification rather than an invented pass threshold.
The statements about minor economic presence and the rest of the industry have no supplied denominator or threshold and cannot be settled merely by grading the two forecasts.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable full-year records place combined compute spending approximately within USD 75–100 billion and combined realized revenue around USD 60 billion. Both numerical components must be assessed independently.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable realized records put either numerical component clearly outside its stated approximate range. A forecast or annualized run rate alone does not qualify.
